chapter: Follow-up questions, Bird and the Ellington sidemen
title: His father teaching Jimmie Lunceford at Le Moine
summary: Jones's father remembered Lunceford as a very nice, classy student before Fisk, but they never stayed in touch.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You mentioned that your father taught English to Jimmie Lunceford.
What did he have to say about Jimmie Lunceford? Did he talk about him?

Yes. When Lunceford died my father was in the hospital at that point, you know, and he was sick himself. He said, "I taught -- James was a very nice boy." This was before Lunceford went to Fisk University. And my father was teaching at Le Moine College in Memphis at that point, you know. It was all in Tennessee. And he said he was a very nice student, very good student. Because Lunceford had a lot of class, you know.
Did they ever stay in touch or did your father ever see him later?
No, I don't think so. I don't think my father realized that he was going to become what he became at that point.
He was quite young, you know.
And consequently they just -- well, after we moved to Chicago there was no way to stay in touch, you know. Geographically we were in two different places, you know.
